first.rationale: Two internal metrics—activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ)—are the more controllable, directly-addressable problems this week, and memory_31 and memory_86 both show durable, unflagged lifts from onboarding/signup simplification on exactly these metrics. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory carries an explicit caveat: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its acquisition/revenue lift estimate is suspect and the intervention risks a margin-eroding race-to-the-bottom that could hurt sustainable qualified revenue even if it wins short-term SMB share. I want to verify memory_73's archived record to see whether the pooled-cohort issue invalidates the SMB-specific lift claim before ever considering it, and verify memory_86 since it's the most directly relevant to the current onboarding-completion drop and I want to confirm the original effect size and population before committing this week's only experiment slot to a related but not identical intervention (onboarding shortening vs. field-cutting). Given single-slot capacity, I'm directing this week's experiment to simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment (not broad rollout, since current conditions differ from when memory_31/86 were generated, and not merely a guarded test, since prior evidence is durable and unflagged) rather than chasing the competitor's pricing move or reviving enterprise/referral levers that don't address the acute activation/onboarding declines.
